newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy's Prodi ready to discuss opposition demands.
newsitem.headline: Italy's Prodi ready to discuss opposition demands.

text.p: Prime Minister Romano Prodi said he was ready to discuss opposition demands to reduce the number of proxy powers included in the budget but not if this meant taking apart the whole package.

The centre-right, led by former premier Silvio Berlusconi, have offered to limit its opposition to the budget, which is currently being examined by parliament, provided the government reduces the number of special powers it is requesting.
"I'm ready to discuss the number of proxy powers provided this doesn't alter the budget, neither in qualitative nor quantative terms," Prodi told parliament.
Berlusconi replied that Prodi was being elusive. "The government is acting against the constitution," he added.
Prodi has asked parliament to give his government numerous special powers to dictate policy on key budget areas, including tax reform.

In the budget, the government has provided a broad outline of the planned fiscal changes. If parliament approves the basic framework, the government can then work out the details without seeking fresh parliamentary approval.

The full lower house of parliament is currently examining the budget and has approved 11 of some 70 articles. It has until November 14 to ratify the whole bill after while the package goes to the upper house (Senate) for a further reading. -- Rome newsroom +396 6782501
